findings.claim: The reworded sfcp-q33 stem says that after the port 'GET /items/abc shows only a generic message because its body has no error field'. That is false under Boot defaults. Boot's default error response for a failed path-variable conversion carries an error field holding the reason phrase. I executed this on JDK 25.0.5.1 with Spring Boot 4.1.2 (spring-boot-starter-webmvc, real embedded server, the stem's ItemController). GET /items/99 gave 404 {"error":"item 99 not found"}, and GET /items/abc gave 400 {"timestamp":"...","status":400,"error":"Bad Request","path":"/items/abc"}. That is the same body the pre-fix stem showed. A front end that 'shows the error text from that body' would therefore show 'Bad Request', not a generic message. The fixer's re-probe used standalone MockMvc, which does not render Boot's /error body, so it could not catch this. The key (D) is still the right fix and the other options are still wrong, but a graded stem now asserts a framework behaviour that is false. A learner who knows Boot's default body meets a contradiction in the premise. The loop-3 leak (sfcp-l3-sme-02) is otherwise fixed: the stem no longer states the 400 status or a conversion failure.
findings.recommendation: Keep the leak fix but make the premise true without stating a 400: for example, '...but GET /items/abc no longer shows id must be a number'. Avoid quoting 'Bad Request', because that reason phrase would re-cue q01 (c). Re-check the key on a real server (not standalone MockMvc), for example with spring-boot-starter-webmvc on a random port.
